items.title: Buddy Collette interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999
items.q: He liked Shelly Manne of course, Shelly was one of the guys, and Andre Previn, but he didn’t know me at all.

ctx.x: Wow. Good deal. When you had a group that you wanted to really get on record, what was it like trying to find a record label here?

Oh well I didn’t really shop that much but what happened is I did a thing for Les Keating, a record with Spud Murphy. I played flute on one of his things. And Les was the kind of a guy that he could hear you and maybe like you, but he was still kind of a little afraid to just take a chance. If he liked you enough he would. He liked Shelly Manne of course, Shelly was one of the guys, and Andre Previn, but he didn’t know me at all. I had no name at the time. But Spud liked me. So Spud said, “Here’s one of the guys…

then when I did the album he didn’t quite like what I had done. That was “A Man of Many Parts,” my first album. It was a great album, and I had a lot of great guys on, but he didn’t know them either. Gerald Wilson playing trumpet, Red Callender on the bass, Larry Bunker, I had a lot of people. Bill Green on the alto and tenor. Jule Grant. These were all great players that I knew but they weren’t names that Les would get excited about. So I guess he thought he had blown it by recording me. He listened to the music…
